q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text:
Yes, ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to an 8-month-old for fever, according to MedlinePlus [6]. It should not be used in children younger than 6 months [6].

Give either paracetamol or ibuprofen if your baby is distressed or uncomfortable, checking the packaging or leaflet to make sure the medicine is suitable, or speaking to a pharmacist or doctor if you are not sure, according to the NHS [3]. Ibuprofen is given every 6 to 8 hours [6], and the dose depends on your child's weight [6]. Do not give ibuprofen if your child is dehydrated, has chickenpox, or has asthma unless a doctor recommends it [2]. Keep breastfeeding as normal and offer plenty of fluids [3].

Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
Give small sips of an oral rehydration solution, according to the SEUP [3]. When he vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give 2–5 ml of oral rehydration solution every 5 minutes for an hour [3]. If he keeps it down, you can slowly increase how often you offer it [3]. Do not use homemade solutions like lemonade or commercial soft drinks [3]. Oral rehydration solutions for children can be bought without a prescription [5].

- Green vomit, blood, or vomit that looks like coffee grounds [7]

- Severe belly pain or headache [7]

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Dehydration happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in, and vomiting is one of the causes [1]. The main risk of vomiting is dehydration, so the priority is to keep fluids going in [3].

When your child vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution: 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour [5]. If they keep it down, you can slowly increase how often you give it [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [5]. Oral rehydration fluids from the pharmacy are the most helpful for mild dehydration [2].

Get help if:
- Vomiting a lot, or not keeping down solids or liquids [6]
- Vomiting even when they take nothing [6]
- Vomit is green, contains blood, or looks like brown coffee grounds [6]
- They seem very low in energy or refuse fluids [3]

If you think your child is severely dehydrated, call your doctor [2].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that keeps a 5-year-old awake all night is often the cough of a viral cold, and in preschool children viral respiratory infections are the main cause of wheeze, according to the SEUP [1]. A cough that is worse at night can also be a sign of asthma, according to the WHO [4].

If your child has been diagnosed with asthma and has a reliever inhaler, give it now, using a spacer, never straight into the mouth, according to the SEUP [7]. If there is no clear improvement, go to a health centre [7].

Get help if:
- Very restless or drowsy, or turning blue or pale [7]
- Breathing gets faster, ribs pull in, or the chest sinks [7]
- Reliever inhalations needed every two hours or less [7]
- Blue colour around the lips [3]

Anyone with asthma symptoms should see a health professional, according to the WHO [4].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last for 10 to 14 days, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Whooping cough also starts like a cold, with a runny nose and mild, occasional cough, and after about a week it can turn into coughing bouts that are worse at night, sometimes with a "whoop" sound or vomiting after coughing, according to the NHS [4].

What to do now: keep offering fluids, and if the air is dry, a cool-mist humidifier or steam from a warm shower may ease the cough. There is no medicine that cures a cold; antibiotics do not help viral coughs.

See a doctor if:
- The cough comes in bouts lasting minutes, or is worse at night [4]
- Your child makes a "whoop" sound or vomits after coughing [4]
- Your child has difficulty breathing, or turns blue or grey [4]
- The cough is getting worse or not getting better [3]

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without a fever, with normal eating, is usually not a sign of anything serious. A high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1].

Keep offering fluids and normal meals; a poor diet for a few days will not hurt, according to MedlinePlus [3]. If a fever does appear, the NHS advises against undressing or sponging your child to cool them, and against covering them in too many clothes [1].

Get help if your child:
- is under 3 months old with a temperature of 38C (100.4 °F) or higher [1]
- is 3 to 6 months old with a temperature of 39C (102.2 °F) or higher [1]
- has a rash along with a high temperature [1]
- has a high temperature lasting 5 days or more [1]
- is not eating, or is not their usual self and you are worried [1]

q: my daughter has red spots all over her stomach and they appeared today
text:
Red spots that appear suddenly and itch can be hives (urticaria), which in childhood are usually caused by an infection rather than an allergy, according to the SEUP [3]. The main sign is raised red patches that move around, fading in one area as they appear in another [3].

Hives can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [5]. If there is swelling around your child's mouth or they are struggling to breathe, call your local emergency number [5].

See your doctor if:
- the spots spread or do not fade [4]
- your child seems unwell or distressed [6]
- the rash comes with a fever [2]

Keep an eye on whether the spots stay raised and itchy or change, and whether your child has any other symptoms.

text:
Spots on the nappy area are common in babies, and nappy rash can usually be treated at home, according to the NHS [2]. Symptoms can include red or raw patches on the bottom or the whole nappy area, and spots, pimples or blisters that may look red or brown [2]. Keep the area clean and dry, change nappies often, and use a barrier cream at each change [2].

See your doctor if:
- the rash is scaly and dry [2]
- the bottom looks itchy or painful [2]
- your baby seems uncomfortable or distressed [2]

q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries are not serious, according to the NHS [2]. The SEUP says the usual symptoms are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1].

What to do now: let him rest, physically and mentally, for 24 to 48 hours depending on how hard the knock was — no sport and no screens during that time, then a gradual return to normal activity [4]. He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. He can eat and drink as usual, according to his appetite [6]. If he has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol at the dose your doctor indicates [6].

Get help now if:
- He was knocked out and has not woken up [2]
- He cannot stay awake or keep his eyes open [2]
- He has a fit (seizure) [2]
- He fell from more than 1 metre or 5 stairs [2]
- Clear fluid or blood from his ears or nose, or bruising behind his ears [2]

Also watch over the first 24 hours for a severe or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion, or difficulty speaking or walking [4].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
At around 6 months, milk still gives most of your baby's energy and nutrients, and how much they eat matters less than getting used to eating, according to the NHS [2]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, following the WHO [3].

Give a variety of foods alongside breast or formula milk, and over time increase the amount and variety until they eat the same foods as the rest of the family in smaller portions [2]. Introduce the different foods one at a time, following your family's usual foods, to diversify the diet [6]. Aim for 2–3 meals a day at 6 to 8 months [3].

Do not give honey, cow's milk or unpasteurised foods before 1 year, and avoid choking hazards like whole nuts, popcorn, sweets and whole grapes [1].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text:
For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula stays the main drink, and the amount of water is not fixed — the AEP says to follow the baby's hunger and fullness cues rather than a set quantity [6]. Offer water in small amounts with meals, and let the baby decide how much [6].

During illness, the WHO says to increase fluid intake, including how often you breastfeed, and to offer soft, favourite foods [1].

If you are worried your baby is drinking too little or too much, or is unwell, ask your doctor.

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: It is common for babies to prefer fruit, and the way to build acceptance of vegetables is to keep offering a wide variety of both, according to the AEP [2]. Offer fruit and vegetables at any of the daily meals and vary how you present them — puréed, mashed or in small pieces [2]. There are no better or worse fruits to start with; it depends on the family's tastes [2]. Taste for different flavours, including bitter ones like some vegetables, is shaped early, and early exposure to different tastes may reduce the risk of refusing new foods [2]. Keep offering vegetables alongside fruit rather than replacing meals with fruit [2]. Whole fruit is preferred over juice: juice offers no nutritional benefit over whole fruit, and a high intake can displace other foods and increase the risk of tooth decay [2].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text:
At 13 months, formula alone is not enough: the WHO recommends breastfeeding continue up to 2 years or beyond, while nutritionally adequate and safe complementary foods are introduced from 6 months [1]. The AEP describes complementary feeding as solid or liquid foods other than breast milk or infant formula, given alongside milk and not as a replacement for it [2].

What to do now: offer her a variety of solid foods through the day alongside her formula, rather than letting formula take the place of meals. The AEP notes that complementary feeding should complement milk, not substitute it [2]. If you are unsure how to move her on from mostly formula, ask your doctor or health visitor for advice on her diet.

Warning signs are not covered by these passages for this situation.

q: how often should a newborn poop
text:
It is normal for a newborn's pooping pattern to vary: the rhythm and consistency of stools differ from one baby to another, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more than a daily stool is the consistency of the poo and whether your baby is comfortable, not a fixed number of dirty nappies [6].

For a baby under 6 months, keep feeding as usual with breast milk or formula — no extra water, juices or fibre [3]. Never give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [3].

See your doctor if your baby has:

- severe tummy pain or is very unsettled and crying a lot [3]
- blood in the stool [3]
- vomiting many times, unable to keep down solids or liquids [3]
- pain when passing stool [3]

Because your baby is under 3 months, ask your doctor about any change in feeding, weight or stools.

q: my 4 year old wakes up coughing only when he lies down
text:
A cough that comes mainly at night or early morning is one of the symptoms of asthma in children, according to MedlinePlus [3]. The SEUP says night-time cough, breathlessness and a whistling sound when breathing out can be signs of an asthma attack, and that in preschool children the usual trigger is a viral respiratory infection [4][5].

If your child is already on asthma medicine, the SEUP says the bronchial obstruction typically improves with bronchodilators such as salbutamol [4].

Get medical help right away if there is:
- Severe coughing or serious breathing problems [3]
- Turning very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails [3]
- The chest pulling in and the ribs and collarbones showing with each breath [5]
- Blue colour around the lips [5]
- Trouble speaking because of breathlessness [5]

Diagnosing asthma in a small child can be difficult, and a doctor may suggest trying asthma medicines for several weeks to see if the symptoms improve, according to MedlinePlus [6].

q: my son has asthma and is using albuterol more than usual
text:
A flare-up of asthma is cough, trouble breathing and wheezing caused by narrowed airways, and it usually gets better with a bronchodilator such as salbutamol, according to the SEUP [1]. Give salbutamol with a spacer (and a mask for small children), never straight into the mouth, because it works less well that way [5]. Most flare-ups are mild and can be treated at home with bronchodilators; symptoms usually settle in a few days but can last up to a week [3]. Get urgent help if:

- Very agitated or drowsy, or turning blue or pale [5]
- Breathing getting faster, ribs or chest pulling in [5]
- Needing inhalations every two hours or less [5]

If there is no clear improvement, go to a health centre [5]. Avoid smoke and, during the flare-up, exercise and allergens [3]. Repeated flare-ups should carry their inhaler to school [3].

q: she is making a strange noise when she breathes but is still smiling
text:
A strange noise when breathing can be a sign of croup, which is an inflammation of the vocal cords and windpipe that causes noisy breathing, a barking cough and a hoarse voice, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It often starts like a cold, and symptoms usually get worse at night and last three to five days [3].

Most viral croup is mild and can be treated at home [3]. If you are worried about your child's breathing, call your doctor right away [3].

Get help if:
- Breathing becomes difficult [3]
- The chest caves in or the ribs pull in with each breath [1]
- Breathing is fast, or they get tired walking or running [1]
- They become floppy, sleepy or very irritable [1]

q: my 6 year old says his chest hurts when he takes a deep breath
text:
Chest pain when breathing deeply can be a sign of asthma, according to the WHO: asthma symptoms include chest tightness that makes it difficult to breathe deeply, and they are often worse at night or during exercise [1]. Symptoms can also be caused by other conditions, so it is worth talking to a healthcare provider [1].

Watch for these signs, which the SEUP says mean you should go to the emergency department: difficulty breathing, with the ribs showing or the chest sinking in, fast breathing, or tiredness when walking or running [2]. Also go if your child becomes limp, sleepy or very irritable [2].

If your child has a cold, the SEUP notes that chest pain when breathing is one of the symptoms to keep an eye on at home [2].

A hard knock to the head can cause headache, confusion, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness, according to the SEUP [1]. Most head injuries are minor, because the skull is hard and protects the brain, but some are more serious, such as a fracture, concussion or brain injury, according to MedlinePlus [4].

- Repeated vomiting or nausea [4]

- Trouble waking her, or unusual irritability [6]

Also seek urgent care if her behaviour or mood worries you, or if the fall was from more than a metre [5].

q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious, according to the NHS [3]. Most febrile seizures do not need treatment [6].

If your child has another seizure: do not move them or try to hold them in place, do not put anything in their mouth, and do not try to lower their temperature by undressing them or sponging them with cold water [5].

Get medical help if your child has a seizure that lasts more than 5 minutes, is having difficulty breathing, has stiffness and twitching on only 1 side of their body, is more sleepy than usual for more than 1 hour after the seizure stops, or has more than 1 seizure within 24 hours [2].

You cannot prevent febrile seizures [6].

q: my 4 year old had a seizure when he was a baby, does that change anything now
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is unlikely to harm your child or cause long-term effects, according to the NHS [2]. Febrile seizures are not the same thing as epilepsy; children who have had one have a slightly increased chance of epilepsy later in life, but this is rare [3].

If your child ever has another seizure, keep them safe while you wait for medical help: check the time it starts and ends, protect their head with your hands or something soft, and remove any dangerous objects nearby [4]. After it ends, put your child in the recovery position and make sure nothing in their mouth or throat affects their breathing [4].

Get medical help if your child has a seizure for the first time, one lasting more than 5 minutes, difficulty breathing, stiffness or twitching on only one side, more sleepiness than usual for over an hour afterwards, or more than one seizure within 24 hours [5].

q: my 7 year old says her neck hurts with a fever

A fever is usually the body's normal response to an infection, and it most often settles within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [1]. A stiff neck with a fever needs urgent medical attention, according to the NHS [7].

q: my child has a sore throat and white stuff on the tonsils
text:
A sore throat with white patches on the tonsils is often tonsillitis, a common childhood illness, according to the NHS [1]. The tonsils look red and swollen, and children may also have a high temperature, cough, headache, earache, trouble swallowing or feel sick [1].

For comfort, the NHS suggests drinking plenty of water, eating cool or soft foods, sucking ice cubes or ice lollies (nothing small and hard for young children, because of choking), and resting [6]. A pharmacist can advise on treatments such as lozenges or throat sprays [2].

See a doctor if the symptoms do not go away within a week, or if throat infections keep coming back [2]. Get help the same day if there are pus-filled spots on the tonsils, or a sore throat so painful it is difficult to eat or drink [2].

Call your local emergency number or go to the emergency department if the sore throat quickly gets much worse, or there is swelling inside the mouth and throat, difficulty speaking, swallowing or breathing, or difficulty opening the mouth — these are signs of quinsy, according to the NHS [3].

q: when should I take my kid to the doctor for a sore throat
text:
Sore throats are very common and usually nothing to worry about — they normally get better by themselves within a week, according to the NHS [5]. Most are caused by viruses like a cold or flu [3].

To help soothe it: give plenty of water, cool or soft foods, and rest [5]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can relieve the pain — ask a pharmacist about these, and always check the leaflet or speak to a pharmacist before giving them [6]. Do not give aspirin to children [1].

See a doctor if:
- Your child is under 5 and needs help for a sore throat [2]
- The sore throat does not improve after a week [2]
- A lump in the mouth or neck, or a mouth ulcer lasting more than 3 weeks [2]

Get urgent help now if your child:
- Is drooling, or cannot swallow [2]
- Has difficulty breathing or a high-pitched sound when breathing [2]
- Has severe symptoms getting worse quickly [2]

q: my son has been scratching his scalp and has white flakes
text:
White flakes on the scalp with itching are common in dandruff, which is not harmful and cannot be caught, according to the NHS [5]. The flakes are often more noticeable in darker hair and if they fall onto the shoulders, and the scalp may feel dry and itchy [5].

Dandruff is not caused by poor hygiene, although it may be more obvious if the hair is not washed regularly [1]. It may be caused by a type of yeast that naturally lives on the skin, or by skin conditions such as eczema, and stress and cold weather can make it worse [1].

Wash the hair regularly, and see your doctor if things do not get better in a month [1].

q: my daughter has a tick attached to her leg
text:
A tick still attached should be removed carefully and the bite cleaned, according to the NHS [6]. Using fine-tipped tweezers or a tick-removal tool, grasp the tick as close to the skin as possible and pull slowly upwards, taking care not to squeeze it or leave any mouthparts in the skin; then clean the bite with antiseptic or soap and water [6].

Watch for early signs of Lyme disease over the following days and weeks, according to the Government of Canada [2]: an expanding rash at the bite site that grows to more than 5 cm over several days, sometimes looking like a bull's eye [2]; fever, chills, fatigue or headache [2]; swollen lymph nodes or muscle and joint aches [2]. Some people do not develop a rash [2].

See your health care provider right away if your daughter develops symptoms of Lyme disease [1]. Tell them where on the body the tick was attached, how long you think it was attached, and where you were when bitten [1].

q: my baby has a temperature of 100.4, is that considered a fever
text:
100.4 °F = 38 °C.

Yes — 100.4°F is 38°C (100.4 °F), and that counts as a fever, according to the NHS [1]. A fever is not an illness in itself; it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [6].

If your baby is under 3 months old, a temperature of 38°C (100.4°F) or higher needs a doctor the same day [5].

For an older baby, you can usually look after them at home, and the temperature should come down over 1 to 4 days [2]. Give plenty of fluids — if they are breastfed, keep breastfeeding as normal — and check on them regularly, including during the night [2]. If they are distressed or uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen, checking the packaging or leaflet to make sure it suits your child; the dose depends on their age and weight, so follow the leaflet or ask a pharmacist or doctor [2].

Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [2].

text:
If your child is under 3 months old and has a temperature of 38C (100.4 °F) or higher, call your doctor the same day, according to the NHS [2].

q: can babies get dehydrated from breastfeeding
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
Breastfed babies can become dehydrated if they lose more fluid than they take in, for example with diarrhoea, vomiting, fever or not feeding enough [1]. Breastfeeding is not a cause of dehydration by itself: breast milk is a fluid, and the WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months [5].

Keep breastfeeding normally, and offer the breast more often if your baby wants it [3]. If your baby is also vomiting, wait 20 minutes after a vomit, then give oral rehydration solution, 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, according to the SEUP [6]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks [6].

Get help if your baby has signs of dehydration such as sunken eyes, little urine, a dry mouth, or vomiting or heavy diarrhoea lasting more than 24 hours [5].

q: should I give my daughter the HPV vaccine
text: The HPV vaccine protects against human papillomavirus (HPV), a common virus spread through skin contact, usually during sex; some types are linked to cervical, mouth, anal, penile, vulval and vaginal cancer, and genital warts, according to the NHS [1]. It works very well at reducing the risk of getting HPV, and since it has been used there has been a big drop in conditions linked to HPV, such as cervical cancer and genital warts [2]. The NHS recommends it for children aged 12 to 13 years old, and for people at higher risk from HPV [1]; in the United States the ages follow the national schedule, so ask your doctor when your daughter is due. The most common side effects are mild and do not last long: swelling or pain where the injection was given, headache, a high temperature, dizziness, feeling sick, tiredness [5]. Serious side effects such as a severe allergic reaction are very rare, and the person who vaccinates your child is trained to treat them immediately [5].

q: my 11 year old needs a tetanus shot after a cut, does he need one
text:
Tetanus enters the body through cuts or wounds, and vaccination is how it is prevented, according to MedlinePlus [1]. DTaP is only for children younger than 7 years old; different vaccines against tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis (Tdap and Td) are available for older children, adolescents, and adults [1]. Because your son is 11, the tetanus-containing vaccine for him would be Tdap or Td, not DTaP [1].

Whether he needs a dose now depends on his vaccination history and the wound, which the sources do not settle. Ask your doctor or the place where he is treated, and tell them if he has ever had a severe allergic reaction to a vaccine protecting against tetanus, diphtheria, or pertussis, or has a nervous system problem such as seizures or Guillain-Barré syndrome [1].

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text:
Malaria's first symptoms are usually fever, headache and chills, and they typically appear 10 to 15 days after the bite of an infected mosquito, according to the WHO [2]. Because these early symptoms are like those of many other febrile illnesses, it is easy to mistake them for something else, so testing as soon as possible is important [2]. If malaria is not treated, P. falciparum malaria can become severe and cause death within 24 hours [2].

Infants, children under 5, pregnant women, travellers and people with HIV or AIDS are at greater risk of severe infection [1]. Severe symptoms include extreme tiredness and fatigue, impaired consciousness, seizures, difficulty breathing, dark or bloody urine, yellowing of the eyes and skin (jaundice), and abnormal bleeding [2]. Anyone with severe symptoms needs emergency care quickly [2]. Early treatment of a mild case can stop the infection getting worse [2].

Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico ese mismo día.

No hay que retrasar las vacunas del calendario por esta reacción: la norma general es mantenerlas sin demoras [2]. Las edades de las vacunas siguen el calendario nacional de Estados Unidos.

Si la fiebre es alta o el niño está decaído, irritable o le cuesta despertarse, llévelo a valoración médica [3].

q: my 18 month old has a fever of 103 and won't take Tylenol
text:
103 °F = 39.4 °C.

A fever is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most children get better within 1 to 4 days, according to the NHS [5]. The main goal is your child's comfort, not bringing the number down by itself [3].

Keep offering plenty of liquids so they stay well hydrated, and dress them lightly in a room that is not too warm [3]. It is normal for them to have no appetite — do not force them to eat [3]. If they will not take Tylenol by mouth, ask your doctor or pharmacist about other options; the dose depends on your child's weight [4].

Get help if:
- They are drowsy or hard to wake [3]
- They are breathing fast or with difficulty [3]
- They have a seizure or fit [5]
- They are not drinking and have fewer wet nappies [3]
- The fever lasts more than 4 days [5]

q: why does my 3 year old have a temperature of 105 degree celsius
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

A temperature of 105 °C is not possible — that reading is almost certainly Fahrenheit, and 105 °F is a high fever. Fever is a sign the body is fighting an infection, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Most fevers in children are caused by infections, and fever itself is not an illness [1].

What to do now: check the temperature with a thermometer, under the arm is fine [5]. If there are no warning signs, start with physical measures — remove extra clothing, offer fluids, reduce activity, and a lukewarm bath only if the child is comfortable [5]. If the fever is causing discomfort, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen; paracetamol is the first choice, according to the PUC Chile manual [4]. The dose depends on your child's weight — use PediBot's dose calculator for paracetamol or ibuprofen.

Get help if:
- Your child is very sleepy, confused, irritable or behaving abnormally [6]
- Severe headache or repeated vomiting [6]
- A seizure happens [6]

q: how long does flu last in toddlers
text:
Most children get better from flu on their own, according to the WHO [3]. The fever and other symptoms usually go away within a week without needing medical care, though the cough can be intense and last two weeks or more [5].

While your child is ill, keep them at home so they don't pass it on, let them rest, and give plenty of fluids [3]. You can treat other symptoms, like fever, and get medical help if symptoms get worse [3].

Flu can be more serious in some children, so seek medical care if symptoms are severe or your child has another medical condition [3]. Children under 5 years are among those at higher risk [3].

q: can my 10 year old take adult Tylenol if I cut it in half
text:
No, do not give your 10-year-old a cut-in-half adult Tylenol. Acetaminophen (Tylenol) helps reduce fever in children and adults, but you need to know how much your child weighs before giving it, according to MedlinePlus [1]. The dose depends on the child's weight, so use the children's product and its weight-based instructions rather than halving an adult tablet.

Paracetamol is a common painkiller for children that helps relieve pain and high temperature, according to the NHS [5]. Check the packet or leaflet to see if it is suitable for your child, and speak to a pharmacist or doctor if you are not sure [3].

Get medical advice if your child has had an extra dose of paracetamol, because it can sometimes be dangerous [6].

q: my 14 year old says her throat hurts really bad when swallowing
text:
A sore throat that hurts when swallowing is usually caused by a virus, like a cold or flu, according to the NHS [4]. Sore throats are very common and normally get better by themselves within a week [5].

To help soothe it: drink plenty of water, eat cool or soft foods, suck ice cubes, ice lollies or hard sweets, and rest [5]. Avoid smoking or smoky places [5].

See a pharmacist if she needs help for a sore throat — they can give the same antibiotic treatment as a GP if it's needed [7]. See a GP if the sore throat does not improve after a week [7].

Ask for an urgent appointment now if she has a very high temperature or feels hot, cold or shivery, or signs of dehydration such as peeing less than usual or dark, strong-smelling pee [7]. Call your local emergency number now if she has difficulty breathing or is unable to swallow, is drooling, or is making a high-pitched sound as she breathes [7].

Fever most often lasts 2 to 4 days, and it can last longer without being more serious [4]. A medicine may not bring it all the way down, and that is common [4].

Get medical help if you have:
- A rash of red spots that do not fade when pressed [4]
- A fever lasting 5 days or more [7]
- Drowsiness, confusion or difficulty breathing [7]

q: my daughter touched a hot pan and has a red patch on her finger
text:

Move your daughter away from the heat and take off any rings or tight clothing near the burn, according to the H. Niño Jesús [3]. Cool the burn under running water for 15 to 20 minutes, then cover it with a clean cloth [3]. Do not put ointment on it and do not break any blisters [3]. You can give paracetamol or ibuprofen for the pain [3].

See a doctor if the burn:
- affects the face, hands or feet [3]
- affects the genitals [3]
- is deep [3]

q: my 9 month old still has no teeth, is that normal
text:
It is common for a first tooth to appear between 4 and 8 months, according to MedlinePlus [4]. Some babies get their first tooth later than that.

Until then, wipe your baby's gums with a damp washcloth after each meal [4]. Do not put your baby to bed with a bottle of milk, juice or sugar water — use only water for bedtime bottles [4]. Start using a soft toothbrush instead of a washcloth as soon as the first tooth shows [4].

Ask your child's health care provider whether your baby needs oral fluoride [4].

q: my child has chickenpox, when can he go back to school
text:
Chickenpox is very contagious, and children usually miss 5 to 6 days of school or childcare because of it, according to the CDC [1]. A person with chickenpox can pass it on until all the lesions have crusted over, according to the PUC Chile manual [2].

While he is ill, keep him comfortable: calamine creams and oatmeal baths can help with the itching, and acetaminophen can help with fever — do not give aspirin, because with chickenpox it can cause Reye syndrome [3].

He can go back once every blister has crusted over [2].

text:
Most head injuries in children are mild and not dangerous, and no tests are usually needed, according to the SEUP [4]. It is important to watch the child for the first 24 hours after the knock for signs of seriousness [4].

If she has a headache, you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol in the dose your doctor indicates [5]. She can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is advisable to wake her every 4 hours [5]. She can keep eating normally, according to her appetite [5]. Most children recover quickly [5].

Get help if:
- Intense or worsening headache, or one that does not improve with the usual medicine [2]
- Repeated vomiting [2]
- Confusion or disorientation; in very small children, irritability or difficulty waking [2]
- Changes in usual behaviour, difficulty speaking or walking [2]
- Blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [2]

text:
No, that is not true: many scientific studies have looked at this and found no link between vaccines and autism, according to MedlinePlus [1]. Vaccines are safe and must go through extensive safety testing and evaluation before they are approved in the United States [1].

Your child gets vaccines at well-child visits, following the vaccination schedule, which lists which vaccines are recommended, how many doses are needed and at what age [4]. In the United States, the CDC publishes that schedule [4]. Following it lets your child build immunity before being exposed to very serious diseases [4].

Keep offering fluids. If your baby is breastfed, keep breastfeeding normally and even more often if they want it, according to the SEUP [1]. If they are having diarrhoea, the most important thing is to prevent dehydration by giving oral rehydration solution that comes already prepared [7].

q: my baby fell off the bed and bumped his head (age: 8 months) (weight: 18 lbs)

18 lb = 8.2 kg.

A bump on the head is a common injury from a fall, and most children recover quickly, according to the SEUP [1][6]. q: my daughter has hives after eating eggs but no trouble breathing
text:
Hives are raised, itchy red patches that come and go, moving from one area of skin to another, according to the SEUP [1]. In childhood, most hives are caused by an infection, and an allergic cause is less common [1]. Hives can come with swelling of the hands, feet, elbows or face, and only exceptionally with trouble breathing or swallowing [1].

If your daughter has hives but is breathing normally, the SEUP says the main symptom is the itchy raised patches themselves [1]. Watch her general condition and whether breathing difficulty appears — ribs pulling in, chest sinking, fast breathing, or tiredness when walking or running [2]. Get urgent help if her general condition worsens, she is listless, drowsy or very irritable, or she has trouble breathing [2].

q: she feels hot but the thermometer says 98.6
text:
A temperature of 98.6°F is normal, not a fever — a high temperature is 38°C (100.4 °F) or more, according to the NHS [1]. A normal temperature varies a little from child to child [1]. If she feels hot but the thermometer reads normal, wait a few minutes and try again, since a bath or too many blankets can raise it briefly [1].

If she does have a fever, the aim is her comfort, not bringing the number down, according to the SEUP [2]. Keep her well hydrated, in a ventilated room at a neutral temperature, and don't over-wrap her [2]. It's normal for her to have less appetite — don't force her to eat [2]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can ease her discomfort, at the dose your paediatrician recommends, every 6-8 hours [2]. Don't alternate them routinely every 3-4 hours [2]. Don't bathe her in cold water or use wet cloths [2].

See a doctor if:
- A rash appears with the fever [7]
- The fever lasts 5 days or more [7]
- She won't eat or isn't her usual self [7]
- She seems dehydrated — fewer wet nappies, sunken eyes, no tears [7]

q: my child has a rash after having a fever, could it be from the fever
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

A rash that appears as the fever drops is typical of exantema súbito (roseola), according to the PUC Chile manual: high fever for 3 to 4 days without other symptoms, then the fever falls and a faint, non-itchy maculopapular rash appears and lasts 48 hours [2]. It is most common between 6 and 18 months, and the diagnosis is clinical, based on that sequence of events [2].

There is no vaccine to prevent it [2]. Keep offering fluids, and treat the fever only if it is causing discomfort, according to the PUC Chile manual [5].

Get help if:
- The child is floppy, barely responsive or very irritable [1]
- Trouble breathing [1]
- Spots that do not fade when pressed [1]
- Refusing all solids and liquids [1]
- Fever lasting more than 5 days [6]

q: what are the side effects of chickenpox shot
text: Most side effects of the chickenpox vaccine are mild and do not last long, according to the NHS [1]. They can include swelling or pain where the injection was given, a high temperature, and a rash at the injection site or more widespread, usually within 1 month of vaccination [1]. Serious side effects, such as a severe allergic reaction, are very rare, and the person who vaccinates your child is trained to treat them immediately [1].

q: my 10 month old is pulling his ear and crying a lot
text:
Ear infections are a common cause of ear pulling and crying in babies, and they often get better on their own within 3 days, according to the NHS [3]. Babies with an ear infection may rub or pull their ear, be irritable or restless, be off their food, or keep losing their balance [3].

For the pain, give paracetamol or ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours for the first 1 to 2 days, before the pain builds up, according to the SEUP [6]. Do not put anything in the ear to soothe the pain, and keep the ear dry, especially if it has been discharging [6]. If your baby is still feeding, frequent saline nose washes can help [6]. It is normal for them to have little appetite, so do not force them to eat [6].

- The pain does not improve or gets worse [3]
- A high temperature [3]
- Discharge running out of the ear [3]

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, painful poops are constipation: the stool is hard and dry and it can hurt to pass, according to MedlinePlus [3]. It usually lasts a short time and is not serious [3].

To help now, offer more liquids, preferably water, and more fiber: cereals and whole-grain bread, fruit and vegetables, according to the SEUP [1]. Do not replace fruit with juice, because juice has little fiber [1]. Keep a regular toilet routine and don't let him hold in the urge to go [1]. Laxatives or enemas should not be given without asking your pediatrician [1].

See your doctor if:
- Bad abdominal pain, or he seems very down and complains a lot [1]
- Blood in the stool [1]
- Vomiting many times, can't keep down solids or liquids [1]

It's not essential that he poops every day; rhythm and consistency vary from person to person [1].

q: my baby is sleeping more today but wakes up and drinks normally
text:
Some babies sleep much more than others, and every baby has their own pattern of waking and sleeping, according to the NHS [1]. Growth spurts, teething and illnesses can all affect how your baby sleeps [2]. If your baby wakes up and feeds normally, that is reassuring.

To keep sleep safe: always put your baby to sleep on their back on a firm, flat mattress [3]. Keep pillows, sheets and blankets away from their face, and do not swaddle them — baby sleeping bags are safer [3]. Keep the room at about 16 to 20C, and check their temperature by feeling their chest or the back of their neck; cool hands and feet are normal [6]. Remove a layer if their skin is hot or sweating [6].

If your baby is having problems sleeping, or you need more advice about getting into a routine, speak to your doctor [2].

text:
Fainting is a sudden, short loss of consciousness that happens when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain, according to the SEUP [2]. Standing still for a long time in extreme heat is one of the situations that can bring it on [2].

- He does not wake up or keeps not responding [3]
- He is pale and limp [3]
- He has jerking movements of the arms or legs [3]

q: my child keeps scratching red patches on his arms
text:
Itchy red patches on the arms are often eczema, which causes dry, itchy skin and is not contagious [1]. It is more common in babies and children, and it can improve or clear up as they grow [1].

To help now: keep the skin moisturised and avoid things that irritate it, such as certain soaps, fabrics and lotions, and stress [1]. Treatments can include medicines, skin creams, light therapy and good skin care [1].

See your doctor if the patches do not get better, or if the skin becomes sore, crusty or infected [3].

- They seem unwell, are losing weight, or are not growing as expected [3]
- They have not had a poo at least 3 times in the last week [6]

A baby who has not had a wet nappy since this morning may be dehydrated, and babies are more likely to become dehydrated because they are more prone to diarrhoea or vomiting, according to MedlinePlus [7]. Signs of dehydration in babies include a dry mouth and tongue, crying without tears, and not wetting nappies for 3 hours or more [6].

Keep breastfeeding normally, and even more often if your baby wants it [1]. Offer fluids often; if your baby struggles to keep them down, oral rehydration solutions for children can be bought without a prescription [4].

Get medical help straight away if there is confusion, fainting, no urine, fast heartbeat or fast breathing [6].

q: my baby is 4 months and has a fever of 38
text:
A fever is the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and most children can be looked after at home while it runs its course [1]. Keep breastfeeding as normal, offer plenty of fluids, and check on your baby regularly, including during the night [1].

If your baby is distressed or uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol — check the packaging or leaflet to be sure it suits your baby, or ask a pharmacist or doctor if you are unsure [1]. Do not give ibuprofen to a baby under 3 months or under 5 kg [7]. Never give aspirin to a child under 16 [7].

Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [1]. Call your local emergency number if your baby:
- has a rash that does not fade when pressed [7]
- has a stiff neck [7]
- is drowsy and hard to wake [7]
- has difficulty breathing [7]
- has a fit for the first time [7]

q: my child got fever after vaccination yesterday
text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day. For an older child, fever in the day or two after a vaccination is a common, expected reaction.

What helps now: offer plenty of fluids and let them rest. If they are uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen — the dose depends on your child's age and weight, so use the dose your doctor or the leaflet gives, or PediBot's dose calculator for these two medicines.

Vaccines are given at well-child visits, following the vaccination schedule, according to MedlinePlus [3]. The ages and doses follow India's national immunisation schedule.

Get help if:
- The fever is high or lasts more than a few days [3]
- Your child is very sleepy, floppy or hard to wake
- They are breathing fast or struggling to breathe
- They have a rash that does not fade when pressed
- They are not drinking or have fewer wet nappies

These are general signs to have your child seen; your doctor can advise on your child's specific situation.

q: my son fell from bed and vomited twice
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomiting after a head injury
text:
A head injury followed by vomiting needs to be checked, according to the SEUP [1]. While you get help, keep him lying on his side and do not give him anything to eat or drink for now [3].

The SEUP lists these signs as reasons to be seen urgently after a head injury: a fall from more than one metre, or a baby under three months [1]. For vomiting, the SEUP says to watch for: vomiting a lot or not keeping down solids or liquids, green vomit, vomit with blood or that looks like coffee grounds, drowsiness or floppiness, much thirst, sunken eyes, crying without tears, or passing little urine [3].

q: my daughter has mosquito bites all over her legs, what can I put
text:
Mosquito bites usually itch and are not usually serious, and they get better in a few days, according to the NHS [2]. For the itch, a zinc and calamine lotion with menthol, phenol or camphor at 0.25 to 0.50%, or a topical corticosteroid such as hydrocortisone for short periods, can be used, according to Ecimed [5]. Insect repellent lotions also relieve bites that are already there [5].

See a doctor if:
- The bites become infected [2]
- There is a serious allergic reaction [2]

The dose of any medicine depends on the child's weight, so ask your doctor or pharmacist [5].

q: my 3 year old is coughing mostly at night, should I use a nebulizer
text:
A night-time cough in a 3-year-old can have several causes, and the sources describe coughing that is worse at night in whooping cough, croup and asthma [1][2][3][4][6]. None of the passages mentions a nebulizer, so there is nothing here on whether to use one.

What the sources do say: for a cough, water can help ease it, whether your child drinks it or you add it to the air with a steamy shower or vaporizer, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Children under four should not have cough medicine [5].

See your doctor if:
- Your child may have croup — the doctor may give medicine to shorten the illness [3]
- Your child is getting worse or not getting better after seeing a doctor [3]
- Asthma symptoms are waking your child at night [6]
- Severe coughing, serious breathing problems, or turning very pale or blue in the face, lips or fingernails — get medical help right away [4]

q: my son has been vomiting since morning and cannot keep ORS down
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Vomits everything and keeps nothing down: it is a danger sign — get seen today
text:
The main risk from vomiting is dehydration, according to the SEUP [6]. Keep giving fluids as oral rehydration solution, in small amounts and often, and continue breastfeeding or formula as usual [7]. If your child is on formula or solids, offer small sips of water too [7]. Do not water down formula, and avoid fruit juice or fizzy drinks, which can make vomiting worse [7].

Get help now if your child:
- vomits a lot and cannot keep down solids or liquids [4]
- is drowsy, floppy, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or pees little [4]
- has vomit that is green, bloody or looks like coffee grounds [4]
- has severe tummy pain or headache [4]

q: मेरे बच्चे को कल से दस्त हो रहे हैं और वह खाना नहीं खा रहा
banner: 💛 यह ज़रूरी है और आप अकेले नहीं हैं। Tele-MANAS 14416 पर कॉल करें (या 112 पर अगर खतरा अभी है)। अगर बच्चे ने खुद को नुकसान पहुँचाया है, तो अभी इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: खानपान के विकार के संकेत
text:
दस्त में ओरल रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्ट (ORS) और ज़िंक सप्लीमेंट दोनों इलाज के मुख्य उपाय हैं, विश्व स्वास्थ्य संगठन के अनुसार [2][4]। ज़िंक दस्त की अवधि लगभग 25% तक घटाता है [2]।

अभी ORS का घोल पिलाइए — साफ़ पानी, नमक और चीनी का मिश्रण [2]। बच्चे को भूखा न रखें: पौष्टिक खाना और स्तनपान जारी रखें, थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार, ताकि उल्टी का खतरा कम हो [2][6]। चिकनी चीज़ें, मिठाई और जूस से बचें; खेल-कूद वाले पेय (स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक) भी न दें [6]।

इनमें से कोई लक्षण दिखे तो डॉक्टर से मिलें:
- मल में खून [3]
- बार-बार बहुत पतली टट्टियाँ या बार-बार उल्टियाँ [3]
- बहुत ज़्यादा प्यास लगना [3]
- बेसुध होना या जागने में कठिनाई [3]
- कुछ भी न पी पाना या स्तनपान न करना [3]

q: मेरे बच्चे को बुखार के साथ लाल दाने निकल आए हैं
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बुखार के साथ लाल दाने कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। खसरा आमतौर पर ज़ुकाम जैसे लक्षणों से शुरू होता है और कुछ दिन बाद दाने निकलते हैं; दाने चेहरे के बालों की लाइन से शुरू होकर नीचे फैलते हैं, और दाने निकलते समय बुखार तेज़ हो सकता है [4]। चिकनपॉक्स में खुजली वाले दाने शरीर पर कहीं भी हो सकते हैं, और उससे पहले या बाद में तेज़ बुखार, दर्द और बेचैनी हो सकती है [5]। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने का मन न करना होता है, फिर मुँह के छाले और हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने आते हैं [3]।

दाने दिखने पर डॉक्टर से बात करें, ख़ासकर अगर आपको खसरा या स्कार्लेट फ़ीवर का शक हो [1]।

अगर दाने उभरे और खुजली वाले हों, तो यह एलर्जी (हाइव्स) हो सकती है और आमतौर पर घर पर संभाली जा सकती है — लेकिन मुँह के आसपास सूजन हो या साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ हो तो तुरंत आपातकालीन नंबर पर कॉल करें [6]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text:
नमस्ते। आपके बच्चे की स्थिति को लेकर मैं समझ सकता हूँ कि आप चिंतित हैं।

SEUP के अनुसार, दस्त या बीमारी के दौरान बच्चे को भूखा नहीं रखना चाहिए, बल्कि सामान्य आहार जारी रखना चाहिए, बस थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में और बार-बार देना चाहिए [1]। स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें, और अगर बच्चा मांगे तो और भी बार-बार कराएं [1]।

अगर बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है, तो यह निर्जलीकरण का संकेत हो सकता है। ऐसे में तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें या नज़दीकी आपातकालीन विभाग जाएं।

SEUP के अनुसार, इन लक्षणों पर ध्यान दें और तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें:
- बहुत उल्टी होना, तरल भी न पचा पाना [1]
- उल्टी हरी, खून वाली या कॉफी जैसी भूरी हो [1]

घर पर ओआरएस (मौखिक रिहाइड्रेशन सॉल्यूशन) थोड़ा-थोड़ा और बार-बार दें।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text: बच्चे को गिरने के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिसके लिए तुरंत आपातकालीन विभाग जाना चाहिए, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [1]। अगर बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा है, या गिरावट एक मीटर से अधिक ऊँचाई से हुई है, तो भी तुरंत अस्पताल जाना चाहिए [1]। अस्पताल में डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करेंगे और देखेंगे कि आगे कोई परीक्षण चाहिए या नहीं, हालाँकि ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी ज़रूरत नहीं पड़ती [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
बच्चे का बहुत रोना कब्ज के कारण भी हो सकता है, ऐसा एनएचएस बताता है [2]। कब्ज में पॉटी करते समय तकलीफ़ होने पर बच्चा रो सकता है।

अगर बच्चा कब्ज के कारण रो रहा है, तो उसे आराम पहुँचाने की कोशिश करें और रोना शांत होने का इंतज़ार करें [1]।

मदद कब लें:
- रोना लगातार हो और शांत न हो, या रोना सामान्य न लगे [4]
- तेज़ बुखार हो या दूध पीना बंद कर दे [4]
- पेट में दर्द के साथ पीलापन, पसीना या सुस्ती हो [6]
- उल्टी हो या मल में खून आए [6]
- 8 घंटे से पेशाब न आए [4]

अगर समझ न आए कि क्या परेशानी है, तो अपने डॉक्टर से बात करें [2]।

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार चढ़ते समय बच्चे का ठंड लगना और हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना सामान्य है, और त्वचा पर जाल जैसा धब्बेदार रूप (क्यूटिस मार्मोराटा) भी खासकर हाथों और पैरों पर दिख सकता है, एसईयूपी के अनुसार [2]। बुखार उतरते समय बच्चा पसीना-पसीना होकर लाल और गर्म हो जाता है [2]।

बुखार का मुख्य लक्षण बेचैनी है, और भूख कम लगना, थकान या सिरदर्द भी सामान्य है [2]। बुखार शरीर का बचाव है, आमतौर पर वायरल संक्रमण से होता है, और इसका मतलब गंभीर बीमारी नहीं है [4]। बुखार में बच्चे को पर्याप्त तरल देना ज़रूरी है ताकि पानी की कमी न हो [1]। दवा की ज़रूरत बुखार के साथ होने वाले लक्षणों पर निर्भर करती है; पैरासिटामोल पहली पसंद है और इबुप्रोफेन भी दिया जा सकता है, पर खुराक बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है [5]।

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है

text:
बहुत कम पेशाब आना अकेले में यह भी हो सकता है कि बच्चा पर्याप्त पानी नहीं पी रहा है — एनएचएस के अनुसार, अगर पेशाब का रंग गहरा हो या उसमें बदबू हो और यही एकमात्र लक्षण हो, तो इसका कारण कम पानी पीना हो सकता है [3]।

पेशाब की मात्रा कम होने पर यूटीआई के बाकी लक्षणों पर भी ध्यान दें, जैसे पेशाब करते समय जलन या दर्द, बार-बार या अचानक तेज़ पेशाब की इच्छा, धुंधला पेशाब, पेशाब में खून, पेट के निचले हिस्से या पीठ में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार या ठंड लगना, बहुत कम तापमान, थकान या कमज़ोरी — एनएचएस के अनुसार [3]।

पानी और तरल पदार्थ खूब दें, खासकर पानी, ताकि दिन में नियमित रूप से पेशाब आए और प्यास न लगे, और गुप्तांगों को साफ़ और सूखा रखें — एनएचएस के अनुसार [4]।

q: मेरी बेटी को तेज बुखार और बैंगनी जैसे दाग हो गए हैं

text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार में उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है [2]।

बड़े बच्चे में तेज बुखार आम बात है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है [3]। तापमान डिजिटल थर्मामीटर से बगल में नापें [3]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें, और ठंडा करने के लिए कपड़े उतारकर स्पंज न करें [2]। 16 साल से कम उम्र के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]। पैरासिटामोल 2 महीने से छोटे बच्चे को न दें, और आइबुप्रोफेन 3 महीने से छोटे, 5 किलो से कम वजन वाले, चिकनपॉक्स या डिहाइड्रेशन वाले बच्चे को न दें [2]। दवा की मात्रा बच्चे की उम्र और वजन पर निर्भर है, इसलिए अपने डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे से पूछें [2]।

त्वचा पर बैंगनी या ऐसे दाग जो दबाने पर न मिटें, गंभीर संकेत हैं [1][2]। ऐसे में तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाएँ [1]।

q: mere 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar 102 hai, paracetamol kitna du
text:
Aapke 3 saal ke bacche ko bukhar hai — paracetamol bukhar aur takleef mein madad karta hai, NHS ke mutabik [1]. Dosis bacche ke wazan par nirbhar karti hai, isliye PediBot ka dose calculator istemal karein [3].

Paracetamol har 4-6 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, din mein paanch se zyada baar nahi [3]. Ibuprofen har 6-8 ghante mein diya ja sakta hai, lekin ise paracetamol ke baad vikalp ke roop mein rakhein [3]. Dawaiyan aapas mein na badlein [3].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Bukhar 38-38.5°C se zyada ho aur bacche ko takleef ho [3]
- Bukhar ke saath daure padne ka itihas ho [3]
- Bacche ko dil, saans, dimag ya metabolism ki koi badi bimari ho [3]

Agar paracetamol ki zyada matra de di gayi ho to turant medical salah lein [7].

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ki khansi asthma ka ek lakshan ho sakta hai, khaas taur par raat mein ya subah jaldi [1]. Bronquiolitis mein bhi khansi kai hafton tak reh sakti hai [5].

Ghar par: khansi ke syrup, mucolytic ya corticosteroid bronquiolitis mein faydemand nahi hain [2]. Bahut saara liquid pilayein aur saaf humidifier ya thande bhaap wala vaporizer istemal karein [6]. Kisi bhi dawa se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochein [6].

Doctor se milein agar:
- Saans lene mein dikkat ya tez saans [6]
- Honton ya chehre par neela rang [1]
- Doodh peene ya khaane mein dikkat (babies mein) [1]
- Bukhaar 4 din se zyada [6]
- Lakshan 10 din se zyada bina sudhaar [6]

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal, ubhre hue dane aur khujli ho sakti hai heat rash (prickly heat) ki wajah se, jo aam taur par harmless hoti hai aur kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jaati hai [6]. Ismein chhote ubhre hue dane, khujli ya chubhan wali feeling aur halki sujan hoti hai [6].

Ghar par kya karein: skin ko thanda rakhein taaki pasina na aaye — dheele cotton kapde pehnayein, halki bedding use karein, thande paani se nahayein, aur dehydration se bachne ke liye khoob paani pilayein [6]. Khujli kam karne ke liye thandi cheez (geela kapda ya ice pack, tea towel mein lipta hua) 20 minute tak lagayein, aur khujlane ke bajaye dane ko thap-thap karein [6]. Perfumed shower gel ya cream use na karein [6].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Munh ke aas-paas sujan ho ya saans lene mein dikkat ho [5]

q: mera bachcha bed se gir gaya aur ek baar ulti ki
text:

Ghar par aaram karaiye aur sir par thanda sekaai dijiye. NHS ke anusaar thande paani ki bottle ya jami hui matar ko towel mein lapet kar kuch der ke liye lagaiye, aaram karaiye aur zaroorat ho to paracetamol de sakte hain [6]. Pehle 24 ghante tak koi bada saath rehna chahiye [6].

q: mere bacche ko kabz hai aur potty karte waqt rota hai
text:
Bacche ka kabz aur potty ke waqt rona aam baat hai, lekin ise theek karne ke liye kuch karna zaroori hai. NHS ke mutabiq, kabz un kuch aam wajahon mein se ek hai jinki wajah se bacche rote hain [3].

Kya karein: bacche ko zyada paani ya doodh pilayein, aur pet par halke haath se maalish karein. Agar baccha doodh peeta hai to breastfeeding ki position theek karein, isse wo araam se potty kar payega [5].

Doctor se kab milein:
- Rona band na ho aur bacche ko shaant na kiya ja sake [7]
- Rona aam rone jaisa na lage [7]
- Bukhar ho ya doodh peena band kar de [7]
- 8 ghante se peshaab na aaya ho [7]
- Skin, hoth ya jeebh neeli, grey ya pale ho [7]

Agar yeh signs hain to turant apne doctor se milein ya emergency department jayein [7].

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A bad night-time cough in a 2-year-old can have several causes, and whooping cough is one of them: it causes coughing bouts that are worse at night and may last for several weeks or months [2]. The coughing fits get worse and happen more often, especially at night, and can last up to 10 weeks or more [3].

If you think it could be whooping cough, ask your doctor for advice, according to the NHS [4]. Keep the room cool and give small sips of water often.

Get help now if:
- Your child's lips, tongue, face or skin turn blue or grey [4]
- They are finding it hard to breathe properly [4]
- They have chest pain that is worse when breathing or coughing [4]
- They are having seizures (fits) [4]
- The cough is very bad and getting worse [4]

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text:
A rash of red spots all over the body in a 5-year-old can have several causes, and the sources describe more than one. Measles causes a widespread rash that usually starts on the face and upper neck and spreads down over about three days, along with fever, runny nose, cough and red, watery eyes, according to the WHO [5]. Scabies can also cause a more widespread rash in young children, especially on the palms, soles and scalp, with intense itching that is often worse at night, according to the WHO [2].

If your child has a rash with swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, fast or difficult breathing, a tight throat or trouble swallowing, skin, tongue or lips turning blue, grey or pale, sudden confusion, drowsiness or dizziness, fainting that cannot be woken, or a child who is limp, floppy or not responding normally, these can be signs of a serious allergic reaction and may need immediate treatment in hospital, according to the NHS [7].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text: It's natural to worry when a child refuses to eat, but what matters is what they eat over a week rather than in a single day, according to the NHS [5]. If your child is active, gaining weight and seems well, they are likely getting enough to eat [5]. Keep offering a variety of foods and try again another time — children's tastes change, and it can take many attempts before a food is accepted [5]. Give small portions, praise them for eating even a little, and don't force or make a fuss if they refuse; just take the food away calmly [2]. Avoid too many snacks between meals — two healthy snacks a day is plenty [2]. See your doctor if your child is not drinking, is drowsy or hard to wake, or has persistent or severe tummy pain [1].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling or wheezing noise with a congested chest in a 6-month-old is often caused by a viral respiratory infection, and in preschool children viral infections are the main cause of wheezing, according to the SEUP [3]. Bronchiolitis is one such infection: it affects the small airways, is caused by viruses (most often RSV), and mostly affects children under 2 [4]. It usually starts like a normal cold with cough and mucus, and after 2 to 4 days breathing difficulty can appear — breathing faster, irritability, feeding poorly, chest noises, ribs pulling in [6].

There is no medicine that cures bronchiolitis; most cases improve within about 2 weeks, though the cough can last longer [5]. Keep feeding them and offer fluids often, and let them sleep propped up semi-upright [5].

While you get help, watch their breathing, how well they feed, their colour and general state, and fever [5].

q: बुखार के लिए कितना पैरासिटामोल दे सकती हूँ?
text: बच्चे का वज़न कितना है? पैरासिटामोल की खुराक उम्र से नहीं, वज़न से तय होती है: वज़न बताइए, फिर सही मात्रा बताई जाएगी।

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
बुखार छोटे बच्चों में बहुत आम है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिन में उतर जाता है, एनएचएस के अनुसार [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान कराती हैं तो सामान्य रूप से जारी रखें, निर्जलीकरण के संकेत देखें, और भूख लगे तो खाना दें [3]। बच्चे को घर पर रखें और रात में भी नियमित रूप से जाँचते रहें [3]। अगर बच्चा बेचैन या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेट या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा उसके लिए ठीक है, या फार्मासिस्ट या डॉक्टर से पूछें [3]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]।

डॉक्टर से सलाह लें अगर: तापमान 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [2]; बुखार के साथ दाने हों [2]; बच्चा खाना न चाहे या अपने सामान्य स्वभाव का न लगे और आपको चिंता हो [2]; निर्जलीकरण हो — जैसे कम गीले नैपी, धँसी आँखें, रोने पर आँसू न आना [2]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाना या स्पंज करना नहीं चाहिए — यह शरीर की प्राकृतिक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, ऐसा NHS कहता है [7]।

बुखार आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में अपने आप सामान्य हो जाता है [1]। बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]। 6 महीने के बच्चे को पैरासिटामोल दी जा सकती है, पर खुराक बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर करती है — PediBot के खुराक कैलकुलेटर से देख सकती हैं [7]। आइबुप्रोफेन 3 महीने से छोटे या 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चे को न दें [7]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- 3 से 6 महीने का बच्चा और तापमान 39C या ज़्यादा [7]
- बुखार के साथ दाने भी हों [7]
- बुखार 5 दिन या ज़्यादा रहे [7]
- बच्चा खाना न चाहे या हमेशा जैसा न लगे [7]
- पेशाब कम आना, धँसी आँखें, रोते समय आँसू न आना [7]

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
सूखी खांसी और सांस लेते समय सीटी जैसी आवाज़ (सिबिलेंस) ब्रोंकियल ट्यूबों में रुकावट से होती है, और प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में इसका मुख्य कारण वायरल श्वसन संक्रमण है, सेविला के यूनिवर्सिटी अस्पताल के अनुसार [2]। ऐसे बच्चों में सिबिलेंस के दौरे बार-बार हो सकते हैं, लेकिन ज़रूरी नहीं कि बड़े होकर उन्हें अस्थमा ही हो [2]।

अभी के लिए: बच्चे को आराम दें और सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ बढ़ने पर तुरंत मदद लें [2]। सिबिलेंस वाली सांस की तकलीफ़ में ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाएँ (जैसे साल्बुटामोल) मदद करती हैं, पर यह दवा डॉक्टर के बताए तरीके और मात्रा से ही दी जाती है [2]।

मदद कब लें:
- सांस लेने में तकलीफ़ या तेज़ सांस [2]
- बच्चा दूध या खाना नहीं ले पा रहा [3]
- खांसी के साथ बुखार और नाक बहना [3]
- होंठ, चेहरा या नाखून नीले पड़ना [7]
- बच्चा सुस्त या चिड़चिड़ा हो जाए [7]

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
बहुत खुजली वाले उभरे हुए दाने छोटे माइट्स के कारण हो सकते हैं जो त्वचा में घुस जाते हैं (स्केबीज़), और अक्सर उंगलियों के बीच एक सिरे पर बिंदु वाली उभरी रेखाएँ दिखती हैं [4]। स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही किया जा सकता है [4]।

स्केबीज़ क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवाओं से ठीक होती है, जो WHO के अनुसार है [2]। इलाज शुरू करने के 24 घंटे तक दूसरों से नज़दीकी संपर्क से बचें [1]। 5 साल या उससे बड़े बच्चे इलाज शुरू करते ही स्कूल जा सकते हैं [1]। इलाज माइट्स को जल्दी मार देता है, लेकिन खुजली कुछ हफ्तों तक रह सकती है [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर:
- त्वचा में संक्रमण लगने का खतरा हो [1]
- कोई और त्वचा रोग, जैसे एक्ज़िमा, हो [1]
- फार्मेसी का इलाज करने के 2 से 4 हफ्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे [1]
- कोहनी, घुटनों, हाथों या पैरों पर पपड़ीदार परतदार दाने हों [1]

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text: हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है: लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के थोड़े-बहुत दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, पर ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और दुष्प्रभावों का मामूली उपचार से इलाज हो सकता है [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना इस बात का संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [6]। टीके समय पर लगवाना ज़रूरी है ताकि बच्चे को सबसे अच्छी सुरक्षा मिले, और अगर कोई टीका छूट गया हो तो अपने डॉक्टर से संपर्क करके उसे पूरा करवाएँ [4]। भारत में एमएमआर सहित टीकों की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi asthma ke lakshan ho sakti hai: bachchon mein asthma se raat ko ya subah jaldi khansi hoti hai [5]. SEUP ke mutabik asthma ke daure mein khansi, saans phoolna aur seene ka dabaav ho sakta hai [1].

Ghar par: kamre ki hawa nam rakhein, saaf humidifier ya thande bhaap wala vaporizer istemal karein, aur bachche ko khoob taral (paani, juice) pilayein [4]. Khansi ya dard ke liye koi bhi dawa dene se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochhein, kyunki kuch cough-cold dawaiyan bachchon ke liye theek nahi hoti [4]. Aspirin bilkul na dein [4].

Turant madad lein agar:
- Saans lene mein takleef ya tez saans [4]
- Hoth, chehra ya naakhun neele ya pale pad jayein [5]
- Seene ki pasliyan andar khinch jayein ya pet zyada hile [7]
- Bahut bechain ya sust ho jaye [7]
- Bukhar 4 din se zyada rahe [4]

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Aapke 8 mahine ke baby ko bed se girne ke baad sar par chot lagi hai — SEUP ke mutabiq yeh golpe, girne ki wajah se hota hai, aur isme sar dard, confusion, chakkar, nausea, ulti aur neend aana jaise lakshan ho sakte hain [1].

Ghar par kya karein: baby ko 24 se 48 ghante aaram karayein, koi physical khel ya screen (tablet, video game, smartphone) na dein [2]. Khana pehle jaisa hi de sakte hain, koi khaas diet zaroori nahi [6]. Agar sar dard ho to paracetamol ya ibuprofen apne doctor ki batayi hui dose mein de sakte hain [6]. Baby so sakta hai, lekin zyada bhaari chot mein har 4 ghante mein jagakar check karein [6].

In lakshon par nazar rakhein aur turant doctor ke paas jaayein:
- Tez ya badhta sar dard, ya jo dawa se theek na ho [2]
- Baar baar ulti [2]
- Bechaini, confusion, ya jagane par na uthna [2]
- Bolne ya chalne mein dikkat [2]
- Naak ya kaan se khoon ya saaf paani [2]

Agar girne ki unchai ek meter se zyada thi, to bhi doctor se milna chahiye [5].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche mein badan par laal daane kai alag-alag bimariyon mein ho sakte hain, aur inmein sabse aam kaaran sankramak hote hain, khaas taur par virus, PUC Chile ke mutabik [6]. Inmein khasoor, khasra, chhoti mata aur rubella jaise virus shamil hain [6].

Ghar par aaram dein aur bachche ko hydrate rakhein. Agar khasoor ho to calamina cream ya oatmeal bath khujli mein madad kar sakte hain, aur bukhar ke liye acetaminophen de sakte hain — aspirin bilkul na dein, kyunki chhoti mata ke saath isse Reye syndrome ho sakta hai, MedlinePlus ke mutabik [4].

Doctor se turant milein agar:
- Saans lene mein dikkat [3]
- Hont ya chehra neela padna [3]
- Bukhar ke saath daane jo dabane par gayab na hon [6]
- Behoshi ya kamzori [6]
- Daane ke saath tez bukhar aur gardan mein akadan [6]

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text:
Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai: polio ke khilaf sabhi bachchon ko pura primovacunation aur teen booster doses milni chahiye, taaki lambi avadhi tak suraksha bani rahe [6]. Polio vaccine aksar difteria, tetanus, tosferina, Haemophilus influenzae aur hepatitis B ki vaccines ke saath mila kar di jaati hai [6].

Bharat ke apne rashtriya immunization program ke tehat polio ki doses bachche ki umar ke hisaab se di jaati hain; apne doctor ya nazdiki health centre se apne bachche ka vaccine schedule zaroor check karwaayein [6].

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text:
Diarrhoea is usually a symptom of an infection in the digestive tract, which can be caused by many different bacteria, viruses and parasites, according to the WHO [6]. It is defined as three or more loose or watery stools a day, or more often than is normal for the child [6].

Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by 25% and reduce stool volume by 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks, and do not give medicines for the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [3].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine or sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Stools so watery and frequent the child cannot drink fast enough [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

हाँ, टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का टीका लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये दुष्प्रभाव आम तौर पर 2-3 दिनों में अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]। खसरे के टीके के मामले में, टीका लगने के 6-7 दिनों बाद हल्का बुखार तथा शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं; इनका इलाज ज़रूरी नहीं, ये अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

टीके के बाद बुखार होने पर, डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. के इंजेक्शन के एक या दो घंटे बाद बच्चे को पेरासिटामॉल की गोली या शर्बत दी जा सकती है, और खुराक के बारे में इंजेक्शन देने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह माननी चाहिए [5]। खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है, जो यहाँ नहीं दी गई है।

डॉक्टर से कब मिलें:
- लक्षण 2-3 दिनों में ठीक न हों [5]
- इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए [5]

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Heat illness can happen when a child is out in the sun too long, and dizziness is one of the signs to take seriously, according to the SEUP [1][3]. Move your child to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, and put cool wet cloths on the forehead, neck and armpits [6]. Offer cool water in small sips, and use a fan to help bring the temperature down [6]. Get medical help now if there is:

- Fever above 39°C that does not come down with home measures [7]
- Loss of consciousness or seizures [7]
- Confusion, trouble speaking or moving [7]
- Persistent vomiting and unable to drink [7]

Do not give fever medicine for heat illness — use physical cooling measures instead, according to the AEPap [5].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text:
Loose stools in a child are usually gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious but can lead to dehydration, according to MedlinePlus [2]. The most important thing is to prevent dehydration by giving oral rehydration solution, according to the SEUP [3].

Give your child oral rehydration solution to replace the fluids and electrolytes lost [4]. Offer it in small amounts often, and keep giving nutritious food, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines to stop the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [3].

Get help if your child has:
- Diarrhoea lasting more than a day [2]
- Any fever in infants, or high fever in older children [2]
- Frequent loose stools or vomiting often [2]
- Signs of dehydration: thirst, dry mouth, no wet nappies for 3 hours or more, no tears when crying [2]
- Blood or pus in the stools, or severe belly pain [2]

q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text:
The MMR vaccine is safe and effective: protection starts within 2 weeks of having it, and after 2 doses around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps, according to the NHS [2]. If mumps occurs after vaccination, symptoms are usually much milder [2].

For children born prematurely, there is no reason to think they respond differently to second-year vaccines, according to the CAV-AEP [1]. However, antibody levels against measles, rubella, mumps and chickenpox are very low or absent in premature babies, especially those born before 28 weeks, so vaccination at 6–11 months may be indicated after exposure, particularly to measles — though this dose does not count as the first scheduled dose [1].

The exact ages and doses for your daughter follow India's national immunisation schedule, so check the timing with your doctor.

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana
text:
Yes, you can give banana. Soft fruits such as banana are listed as good finger foods, according to the NHS [5].

At 6 months, start with finger foods that break up easily in the mouth and are long enough for your baby to grip — pieces about the size of your own finger work well [5]. Offer finger foods at each meal, and give sips of water with meals from an open or free-flow cup [4][5].

Avoid hard foods, such as whole nuts or raw carrots and apples, to reduce the risk of choking [5].

If your baby was born prematurely, ask your health visitor or GP when to start solids [3].

q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Stomach pain and constipation often go together: constipation can cause a stomach ache and a bloated or sick feeling, according to the NHS [1]. Abdominal pain is a common symptom in children and most causes are benign and self-limiting, such as constipation, according to the SEUP [2].

What to do now: increase fluids, preferably water, to soften the poo and make it easier to pass, and add more fibre-rich meals — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables. Do not replace fruit with juices, as juices have little fibre [3]. Most cases improve with these diet changes, and sometimes with a laxative if a paediatrician prescribes one [3]. Do not give laxatives or enemas without asking your paediatrician [3].

See a doctor if:
- Severe abdominal pain, or the child is very down and complaining a lot [3]
- Blood in the stools [3]
- Vomiting many times, unable to keep down solids or liquids [3]
- Pain that is intense and continuous, with the child generally unwell [4]

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text:
At around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets all your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are needed as well, according to the WHO [3]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows [3]. Offer food before the usual milk feed, when your baby is not too tired or too hungry, and let them set the pace [1]. Keep offering different foods, even ones already rejected — it can take 10 tries or more before a new food is accepted [1]. Breast milk or first infant formula stays the main drink in the first year; do not give whole cows', goats' or sheep's milk as a main drink before 1 year [1]. From around 6 months, offer sips of water with meals from an open or free-flow cup [1].

Get help if:
- Your baby is not gaining weight or is losing weight [3]
- Feeding is painful or difficult for your baby [1]

A severe cough with catarrh (a runny nose) can be the first phase of whooping cough, which usually lasts 1 to 2 weeks and looks like a cold, according to the Gouvernement du Canada [4]. The cough then becomes more severe, in fits that can make it hard to breathe [4].

Whooping cough generally occurs in 3 phases and can last 6 to more than 12 weeks [4]. For older children and those who have been vaccinated, the symptoms may be less severe [4].

Treatment depends on your child's age and how long they have had the infection, according to the NHS [6]. If whooping cough is diagnosed within 3 weeks of the cough starting, antibiotics are given to help stop it spreading to others, though they may not reduce symptoms [6]. Hospital treatment is usually needed for severe whooping cough [6].

Get help if your child:
- has breathing difficulties [2]
- has fits (seizures) [2]
- is not drinking enough or seems dehydrated [2]
- has a lung infection [5]

text:
Watery stools with weakness in a young child is usually gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious but can sometimes lead to dehydration, according to MedlinePlus [3].

Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the diarrhoea and reduce stool volume, according to the WHO [1]. - Diarrhoea lasting more than a day [3]

q: what can I give my 2 year old for diarrhoea
text:
For diarrhoea in a young child, the main treatment is oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools, according to the WHO [1]. Zinc supplements are also a key measure: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and cut stool volume by about 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1].

Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses; use oral rehydration solutions that come already prepared, according to the SEUP [3]. Do not give your child medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without consulting your paediatrician [3].

Get help if:
- Much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes [3]
- Marked irritability, drowsiness or reduced responsiveness [3]
- Stools so liquid and frequent that the child cannot drink fast enough [3]
- Refusing to eat or drink [3]
- Persistent or intense abdominal pain, or stools with a lot of blood [3]
